english.title: Produce a programme with threatening visual image / sound intending to stir up religious / sexual orientation hatred
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) produced a programme, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PROGRAMME..), which involved threatening visual images or sounds, intending thereby to stir up

(A)_[religious hatred]_
(B)_[hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation]_

and which were included in a programme service
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 29F(1), (2)(b) and 29L(3) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution of this offence.
(ii) See also H8428 (provide such programme service), H8430 (directing such programme service), and H8431 (using offending words/behaviour).
(iii) Section 29L(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that for purposes of the rules against charging more than one offence in the same count or information, each of sections 29B to 29G creates one offence.
(iv) This offence was inserted into the Public Order Act 1986 by the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006 and amended to include "hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation" as from 23/03/2010 by Sch 16 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Until the introduction of section 154 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to Twelve months is to be read as six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
